blocks.intro: Switch between before and after a tune-up. The brown patches, the soaked spot and the numbers all come from where the water lands.

This is why turning the timer up rarely fixes a brown spot.

blocks.title: What it is doing, and **what usually causes it.**
blocks.intro: A short guide to the calls we get most. It is a starting point: the visit is where we confirm it.

items.title: Usually a valve or a wire
items.body: A solenoid that has failed, a wire nicked by a shovel or an edger, or a controller station that has quit. We test each one until we find it.

items.title: Usually grit in the valve
items.body: A bit of debris under the valve diaphragm holds it open. Cleaning or rebuilding the valve fixes most of these without digging.

items.title: A broken head or riser
items.body: A mower, a car tire or a hard frost cracks the head or the short pipe under it. Water comes straight up, and the rest of the zone runs weak.

items.title: Coverage, not run time
items.body: A head that is tilted, sunk or clogged leaves a gap between heads. Fixing the head fixes the patch. More minutes only flood the rest.

items.title: Pressure, or a hidden leak
items.body: A partly closed shutoff, a leaking line under the turf or too many heads on one zone. We check pressure and walk the line.

items.title: A slow leak underground
items.body: Turf that stays wet, sinks or grows faster in a stripe often sits over a cracked fitting. We dig small, fix it and put the sod back.

steps.title: Every zone, run and watched
steps.body: We start at the controller and run each zone in turn, so we see the problem you called about and anything else that is quietly wasting water.

steps.title: The cause, found
steps.body: A dry spot gets traced to its head, a dead zone to its valve or wire, a soggy stripe to its leak.

steps.title: You hear it first
steps.body: Before we fix anything, we tell you what we found and what it takes. You decide.

steps.title: Fixed, tested, put back
steps.body: Repairs done, the zone run again to prove it, heads aimed, and the turf put back so the repair is hard to find.

blocks.eyebrow: Why it is worth fixing now
blocks.figureLabel: gallons a run from one broken head, in our example
blocks.title: One broken head **adds up fast.**
blocks.body: A cracked head or riser can let five gallons a minute or more run straight into the ground. On a 20 minute zone that is over 100 gallons a run, into one spot, while the rest of that zone runs weak. Three runs a week, all summer, and it shows up on the water bill or the well pump.

blocks.title: Sprinkler repair **in your town.**
blocks.intro: Each town has its own page with the details for that area.

faq.q: Do you repair sprinkler systems you did not install?
faq.a: Yes. Most of what Misty's does is service and repair, whoever put the system in. If a part is no longer made, we will tell you what fits and what it takes.

faq.q: One part of my lawn is brown but the sprinklers run every day. What is wrong?
faq.a: Almost always coverage. A head near the brown spot is tilted, sunk below the grass, clogged or broken, so the water never reaches it. Turning up the run time floods the rest of the lawn and still misses the spot. Fixing the head is the fix.

faq.q: A zone will not shut off. What should I do?
faq.a: Turn the system off at the controller first. If water still runs, close the main shutoff to the irrigation, usually a valve in the basement near where the line leaves the house. Then call or text [(810) 423-9513](tel:+18104239513). A stuck valve is usually grit under the diaphragm, and it is often a quick fix.

faq.q: How do I know if there is a leak underground?
faq.a: Look for a patch that stays soggy, turf that sinks, a stripe that grows faster and greener than the rest, or a valve box with water standing in it. A zone that runs weak at every head can also mean a leak. We find it by running the zone and walking the line.

faq.q: Can you fix a head the mower hit?
faq.a: Yes. That is one of the most common repairs we do. Usually the head or the riser under it is cracked. We replace it, set it level with the turf so the mower rides over it, and aim it. More on [heads and nozzles](/sprinkler-head-replacement/).

faq.q: My controller says a station has a fault. Is that the controller or the yard?
faq.a: Usually the yard: a failed solenoid on the valve, or a cut or corroded wire between the valve and the controller. We test the station and the wire to find which. If it is the controller, see [controller installation and setup](/sprinkler-controllers/).

faq.q: Should I fix a broken head now or wait until next season?
faq.a: Now, if the system is still running. A broken head wastes water every run, and the rest of that zone runs weak, so the lawn browns around it. If it is late in the year, we can fix it at your [spring startup](/sprinkler-startup/) instead.
